name: Phase 0 · Technical foundations
goal: Understand how computers, operating systems and networks actually work before studying advanced security.

modules.title: Computer Architecture and OS Internals
modules.whyMatters: Understand CPU, memory, processes, kernel and system calls. This makes malware analysis, exploit research and forensics intelligible.
modules.topicsStr: CPU architecture; Von Neumann and Harvard models; ALU, control unit and registers; instruction cycle; ISA; x86/x64 and ARM overview; binary, hexadecimal and endianness; RAM and cache; stack and heap; virtual memory, paging and page tables; MMU; interrupts; user mode and kernel mode; system calls; processes and threads; scheduling and context switching; IPC; filesystems; drivers; boot process; BIOS/UEFI; Secure Boot and TPM.
modules.booksStr: OSTEP chapters: processes, process API, direct execution, scheduling, address spaces, memory API, address translation, paging, TLBs, concurrency and file systems. OST2: architecture and x86-64 foundations. Microsoft Sysinternals: Process Explorer, Process Monitor and Autoruns.
modules.coursesStr: Hackers-Arise: Getting Started Becoming a Master Hacker (orientation only). OST2: architecture and assembly foundations. HTB Academy: relevant OS and information-security foundation modules.
modules.practicalStr: Draw CPU and OS diagrams; inspect process trees with Process Explorer and Linux ps; observe file/process activity with Procmon; use strace on a benign Linux process; explain virtual memory and user/kernel transitions.
modules.deliverable: A labelled architecture diagram, process lifecycle diagram, notes and a short comparison of Windows and Linux process behaviour.

commands.desc: Trace file, process, and socket system calls
Inspect CPU microarchitecture and flags
View virtual memory regions, memory protections, and mapped files
View top 10 memory-consuming processes
Headless Sysinternals Procmon capture

subtopics.title: CPU Microarchitecture & Registers
subtopics.detail: General purpose registers (RAX, RBX, RCX, RDX, RSI, RDI, RSP, RBP, R8-R15), RIP, instruction cycle (Fetch, Decode, Execute, Writeback).

subtopics.title: Virtual Memory & MMU Paging
subtopics.detail: Paging structures (PML4, PDPT, PD, PT), Page Table Entries (PTE), CR3 register, Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB), Page Faults (#PF).

subtopics.title: Process & Thread Execution Lifecycle
subtopics.detail: EPROCESS / task_struct, threads, context switching overhead, Thread Local Storage (TLS), kernel/user mode transitions via SYSCALL.

knowledgeAssessment: Explain the difference between a physical address and a virtual address.
What happens during a context switch between two threads in different processes?
How does the CPU transition from User Mode (Ring 3) to Kernel Mode (Ring 0)?
What security boundary does the MMU enforce?

modules.title: Networking and Protocol Internals
modules.whyMatters: Learn how systems communicate and how to read network evidence. This supports reconnaissance, APT infrastructure analysis, incident response and network testing.
modules.topicsStr: OSI and TCP/IP; Ethernet and MAC; ARP; IPv4/IPv6; subnetting and CIDR; routing and switching; NAT; VLAN; ICMP; TCP and UDP; ports and sockets; TCP handshake and teardown; DNS; DHCP; HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3; TLS handshake and certificates; SMTP, IMAP and POP3; SSH, RDP, SMB, LDAP, Kerberos, NTP and SNMP; proxies and VPNs; packet headers; fragmentation; PCAP; flow data; Zeek and Suricata telemetry.
modules.booksStr: Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach: Internet, application, transport, network and link layers, wireless networks and network security. Read relevant RFCs when studying a protocol.
modules.coursesStr: Hackers-Arise: Network Basics for Hackers; Nmap for Hackers. HTB Academy: Networking Fundamentals and relevant enumeration modules. TryHackMe: Pre Security networking content.
modules.practicalStr: Use Wireshark to inspect DNS, TCP handshake, TLS and HTTP; analyse supplied PCAPs; map a small private lab network; compare packet evidence with Zeek logs.
modules.deliverable: 20 annotated packet captures or protocol notes, subnetting exercises and a network diagram.

commands.cmd: tcpdump -i eth0 -nn -s0 -w capture.pcap 'port 53 or port 80 or port 443'
commands.desc: Capture DNS and web traffic without truncating packets
Display IP conversation statistics from PCAP
Extract all DNS queries made in capture
Generate protocol-specific structured Zeek log files
Inspect TLS handshake and certificate chain details

subtopics.title: Layer 2 & Layer 3 Internals
subtopics.detail: Ethernet framing, ARP poisoning mechanisms, IPv4 header flags and fragmentation, IPv6 SLAAC and routing tables.

subtopics.title: Transport Layer: TCP vs UDP
subtopics.detail: 3-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK), sequence numbers, sliding windows, retransmission, 4-way teardown (FIN/RST), UDP socket mechanics.

subtopics.title: Application Protocols & Telemetry
subtopics.detail: DNS record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT, MX), HTTP/1.1 keep-alive vs HTTP/2 multiplexing, TLS 1.3 handshake cryptographic exchanges.

knowledgeAssessment: Describe how TCP sequence numbers prevent blind packet injection.
What is the difference between ARP spoofing and DNS cache poisoning?
How does SNI (Server Name Indication) in TLS handshakes leak hostnames?
What information does a NetFlow / IPFIX flow record contain compared to full packet capture?

modules.title: Linux Internals and Administration
modules.whyMatters: Build Linux administration and internals knowledge for system security, malware research, incident response and authorised infrastructure assessment.
modules.topicsStr: Distributions and kernel/user space; filesystem hierarchy; shell and Bash; users and groups; ownership, permissions and ACLs; sudo; packages; systemd; processes, jobs and signals; cron; environment variables; /proc and /sys; system calls; ELF; shared libraries and dynamic linking; PAM; SSH; capabilities; namespaces and cgroups; networking; nftables and iptables; auditd and journald; AppArmor and SELinux; kernel modules; containers; hardening and log review.
modules.booksStr: Linux Journey for basics; The Linux Command Line for shell and filesystem; Linux kernel documentation for internals; Bash manual for scripting. Read about permissions, process management, services, logs and namespaces.
modules.coursesStr: Hackers-Arise: Linux Basics for Hackers, Linux Firewalls, Advanced Linux for Hackers and Privilege Escalation. HTB Academy: Linux Fundamentals and Linux Privilege Escalation. TryHackMe: Linux Fundamentals.
modules.practicalStr: Build one Linux VM; practise users, permissions, services, SSH, firewall, logs, process inspection and safe system auditing. Use strace on benign programs.
modules.deliverable: Linux administration notebook, hardening checklist and a small system-audit script.

commands.desc: Locate all SUID binaries on filesystem
Find all binaries with Linux file capabilities set
Inspect systemd journal logs for SSH daemon
List all listening TCP and UDP sockets with owning process IDs
Inspect ELF file header and program load headers

subtopics.title: Linux Privilege Model & DAC/MAC
subtopics.detail: POSIX user/group permissions, SUID/SGID bits, ACLs, Linux Capabilities (cap_net_raw, cap_sys_admin), SELinux contexts and AppArmor profiles.

subtopics.title: Systemd, Daemons & Service Isolation
subtopics.detail: Unit files, dependencies, target states, cgroups v2 resource limiting, mount namespaces and container isolation.

subtopics.title: Kernel / User Space Interface & Telemetry
subtopics.detail: /proc virtual filesystem, /sys hardware tree, auditd syscall logging, eBPF tracing probes.

knowledgeAssessment: Explain the difference between SUID root and granting a capability like CAP_SETUID.
How does systemd journald correlate log entries with specific unit files?
What is the function of the /proc/sys/kernel/randomize_va_space knob?
Explain how Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) handle authentication chains.

modules.title: Windows Internals and Administration
modules.whyMatters: Understand Windows processes, security boundaries, registry, authentication and telemetry. This is essential for enterprise APT and AD work.
modules.topicsStr: Windows architecture and boot; kernel and executive; user/kernel mode; processes, threads, handles and tokens; SIDs; ACL, DACL and SACL; registry; services; NTFS and ADS; SAM and LSA concepts; LSASS security; authentication; Event Logs; ETW; Sysmon; PowerShell; WMI and CIM; Task Scheduler; Defender; firewall; AppLocker and WDAC; DLL loading; PE format; memory management; Windows auditing and hardening.
modules.booksStr: Windows Internals, Parts 1 and 2: system architecture, processes/threads, memory, security, I/O and storage. Microsoft Learn: Windows security, Sysinternals, PowerShell and event logging.
modules.coursesStr: Hackers-Arise: PowerShell for Hackers. HTB Academy: Windows Fundamentals and Windows Privilege Escalation foundations. TryHackMe: Windows fundamentals rooms.
modules.practicalStr: Install Sysmon on a Windows VM; inspect Event Viewer; use Process Explorer, Autoruns and Process Monitor; review PowerShell logs and Windows security settings.
modules.deliverable: Windows internals notebook, Sysmon configuration and an event-investigation report.

commands.desc: Query Sysmon Process Creation events (Event ID 1)
Display current user SID, security group memberships, and token privileges
Query Windows Security Event Log for recent successful logons
Inspect Windows service binary path, startup type, and service account
Detect Alternate Data Streams (ADS) on NTFS files

subtopics.title: Windows Access Tokens & Integrity Levels
subtopics.detail: Primary vs Impersonation tokens, Token Privileges (SeDebugPrivilege, SeImpersonatePrivilege), Integrity Levels (Untrusted, Low, Medium, High, System), Token Stealing concepts.

subtopics.title: Object Manager & Security Descriptors
subtopics.detail: Executive objects, handles, Security Identifiers (SIDs), Discretionary ACL (DACL), System ACL (SACL), Access Mask calculation.

subtopics.title: PE Structure & DLL Search Order
subtopics.detail: DOS Header, NT Headers, Section Headers (.text, .data, .rsrc, .reloc), Import/Export Address Tables (IAT/EAT), DLL search order hijacking.

knowledgeAssessment: What is the difference between a DACL and a SACL in a Windows Security Descriptor?
How does an impersonation token differ from a primary process token?
What role does LSASS play in Windows authentication, and why is it a primary target?
Explain how ETW (Event Tracing for Windows) delivers telemetry to EDR agents.

name: Phase 1 · Programming and low-level engineering
goal: Build the ability to automate analysis, understand scripts and inspect compiled programs.

modules.title: Python for Cybersecurity
modules.whyMatters: Automate repeatable research and defensive analysis tasks; understand data handling and APIs.
modules.topicsStr: Syntax, types, control flow, functions, collections, modules, packages, exceptions, file handling, JSON/CSV/XML, regex, OOP, iterators, generators, virtual environments, sockets, HTTP clients, APIs, subprocess, logging, testing, async, concurrency, binary parsing and data analysis.
modules.booksStr: Python official tutorial; Automate the Boring Stuff chapters on files, regex, web/API interaction, spreadsheets and automation; Real Python for deeper concepts.
modules.coursesStr: Hackers-Arise: Python Basics for Hackers, Scripting for Hackers, Advanced Python for Hackers. HTB Academy: Introduction to Python or equivalent current modules.
modules.practicalStr: Build a log parser, IOC normaliser, hash utility, PCAP metadata extractor and report generator using safe sample data.
modules.deliverable: Four documented Python utilities with tests and usage instructions.

commands.desc: Create and activate isolated Python virtual environment
Parse PE headers and section characteristics in CLI

commands.cmd: pip install scapy requests pefile pytest black
commands.desc: Install standard Python security analysis toolchain
Execute automated unit tests with verbose reporting

subtopics.title: Binary Parsing & Raw Struct Unpacking
subtopics.detail: struct module, binary pack/unpack, big-endian vs little-endian, parsing custom file headers and network protocols.

subtopics.title: Network Scripting with Sockets & Scapy
subtopics.detail: Raw socket manipulation, constructing TCP/IP packets with Scapy, sniffing PCAP streams, analyzing DNS requests programmatically.

subtopics.title: Threat Intelligence & API Automation
subtopics.detail: REST APIs with requests/aiohttp, rate limiting, JSON schema validation, normalizing IOCs into STIX 2.1 objects.

knowledgeAssessment: How do you safely unpack a 32-bit little-endian integer from a binary stream in Python?
Explain the difference between synchronous requests and async event-driven HTTP querying.
How does pefile locate the Import Address Table of an executable?
Why is input sanitization critical when using Python's subprocess module?

modules.title: PowerShell and Bash Automation
modules.whyMatters: Automate administration and collect system evidence reliably.
modules.topicsStr: PowerShell objects and pipeline; cmdlets; variables; functions; modules; error handling; CIM/WMI; registry; Event Logs; processes and services; remoting concepts; script signing and logging. Bash variables, quoting, pipelines, functions, exit codes, text processing, process control and scheduled jobs.
modules.booksStr: Microsoft PowerShell learning paths and reference; GNU Bash manual; explainShell to understand command syntax.
modules.coursesStr: Hackers-Arise: PowerShell for Hackers and Scripting for Hackers. Reinforce with Microsoft Learn and Bash manual.
modules.practicalStr: Create an endpoint inventory collector, event-log parser and Linux configuration-audit script. Run only on owned lab machines.
modules.deliverable: Scripts with README, safe test data, error handling and sample output.

Audit all scheduled cron jobs and permissions
Lint Bash script for subtle bugs, quoting mistakes, and security risks

subtopics.title: PowerShell Object Pipeline & CIM Queries
subtopics.detail: Pipeline passing .NET objects rather than strings, WMI repository architecture, CIM sessions, Script Block execution.

subtopics.title: PowerShell Security Controls & Telemetry
subtopics.detail: Execution Policy (and why it is not a boundary), Constrained Language Mode, Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104), Transcription.

subtopics.title: POSIX Bash Scripting & Stream Processing
subtopics.detail: Subshells, file descriptors (stdin/stdout/stderr), parameter expansion, sed/awk text filtering, cron and systemd timer syntax.

knowledgeAssessment: Why is PowerShell's object pipeline fundamentally more reliable for automation than Bash text streams?
How does PowerShell Script Block Logging defeat obfuscation?
What is the difference between $() command substitution and backticks in Bash?
How do you handle error trapping and non-terminating errors in PowerShell ($ErrorActionPreference)?

modules.title: C, C++ and Assembly
modules.whyMatters: Understand memory, compiled code and low-level behaviour needed for reverse engineering and vulnerability research.
modules.topicsStr: C types, pointers, arrays, strings, structs, unions, memory allocation, stack/heap, compilation and linking; C++ classes, references, RAII, smart pointers, templates and STL; binary/hex, registers, x86/x64 instructions, addressing, stack frames, calling conventions, control flow, debugging and disassembly.
modules.booksStr: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective: information representation, machine-level programming, processor architecture, linking, exceptional control flow, virtual memory, system I/O and networking. OST2 assembly courses.
modules.coursesStr: Hackers-Arise: x86 Assembler Language; Exploit Development Part I and II only after C and assembly foundations. OST2: x86-64 and low-level programming. pwn.college for structured practice.
modules.practicalStr: Compile benign C programs, inspect assembly in Compiler Explorer, debug with GDB and map stack/heap layouts in toy programs.
modules.deliverable: Annotated source-to-assembly examples and a debugger walkthrough report.

commands.desc: Compile toy binary with debugging symbols and disabled protections for analysis
Disassemble main function in Intel syntax
Launch GDB, set breakpoint at main, run and display register state
Analyze heap memory leaks and buffer over-reads

subtopics.title: Pointers, Memory Allocation & Memory Model
subtopics.detail: Pointer arithmetic, double pointers, stack allocation vs heap (malloc/free), memory leaks, dangling pointers, struct packing.

subtopics.title: x86-64 Assembly & Calling Conventions
subtopics.detail: System V AMD64 ABI (RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, R9) vs Microsoft x64 (RCX, RDX, R8, R9, Shadow Space), stack alignment, prologue/epilogue.

subtopics.title: Compilation, Linking & Debugging
subtopics.detail: Pre-processor, compilation to assembly, object file creation, dynamic vs static linking, symbol tables, GDB memory examination.

knowledgeAssessment: Explain what happens to RSP and RBP when a CALL instruction is executed.
What is the difference between Microsoft x64 and System V AMD64 calling conventions?
Why is an out-of-bounds pointer write to the stack dangerous for control flow?
How does RAII in C++ prevent resource leaks compared to manual C memory management?

name: Phase 2 · APT research and Cyber Threat Intelligence
goal: Learn to investigate threat actors, campaigns, infrastructure and reported behaviour using evidence and confidence levels.

modules.title: APT Fundamentals and MITRE ATT&CK
modules.whyMatters: Understand adversary motivations and translate public reporting into structured intelligence.
modules.topicsStr: APT vs cybercrime; state-sponsored and financially motivated threats; campaigns vs intrusions; actor aliases; malware families; TTPs; attribution limits; false flags; intelligence lifecycle; strategic/operational/tactical/technical CTI; source reliability; confidence; ATT&CK tactics, techniques, sub-techniques, groups, software, campaigns, mitigations and detection strategies; Kill Chain; Diamond Model; Pyramid of Pain; STIX/TAXII.
modules.booksStr: MITRE ATT&CK: read Enterprise matrix, tactics, techniques, groups, software, campaigns, mitigations and detection strategies. Study analytic confidence and source quality. CISA advisories and public vendor reports for evidence.
modules.coursesStr: Hackers-Arise: Cyber Threat Intelligence for Hackers; MITRE ATT&CK Framework for Security Analyst. Supplement with MITRE CTI training and HTB/THM relevant CTI rooms.
modules.practicalStr: Map public campaign reporting to ATT&CK; record source URL, quoted behaviour, technique rationale and confidence; build an ATT&CK Navigator layer.
modules.deliverable: One actor profile, one campaign timeline, ATT&CK layer and evidence register.

commands.desc: Query MITRE CTI STIX repository via CLI
Query MISP threat sharing instance for matching IOCs
Validate STIX 2.1 compliance of threat intelligence export

subtopics.title: Threat Actor Models & Intelligence Frameworks
subtopics.detail: Lockheed Martin Cyber Kill Chain, Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis (Adversary, Capability, Infrastructure, Victim), Pyramid of Pain.

subtopics.title: MITRE ATT&CK Structure & Taxonomy
subtopics.detail: 14 Tactics (Initial Access to Impact), Techniques, Sub-techniques, Data Sources, Mitigations, and Behavioral Detections.

subtopics.title: Analytical Confidence & Attribution Rigor
subtopics.detail: Admiralty Code / Source Reliability (A-F) & Credibility (1-6), Analysis of Competing Hypotheses (ACH), avoiding false flags.

knowledgeAssessment: Explain why TTPs are at the apex of David Bianco's Pyramid of Pain.
How does the Diamond Model model pivoting between infrastructure and capabilities?
What distinguishes Strategic Threat Intelligence from Tactical Threat Intelligence?
How do you evaluate source reliability when reviewing a commercial threat intelligence report?

modules.title: OSINT and Threat Infrastructure Analysis
modules.whyMatters: Collect and correlate public information about domains, IPs, certificates and exposed infrastructure without intrusive access.
modules.topicsStr: Search operators; source validation; WHOIS/RDAP; DNS; passive DNS; certificate transparency; ASN; IP reputation; hosting; URL analysis; public code repositories; metadata; public documents; Shodan/Censys; relationship graphs; infrastructure pivoting; collection ethics and reporting.
modules.booksStr: Open Source Intelligence Techniques by Michael Bazzell: search, public records, domain/infrastructure, social media, metadata, verification and reporting. Read official tool documentation.
modules.coursesStr: Hackers-Arise: Ultimate OSINT Beginner, Open Source Intelligence, Remaining Anonymous. HTB Academy: Footprinting and Reconnaissance. Tools: Amass, Subfinder, Shodan, Censys, Maltego, SpiderFoot and crt.sh.
modules.practicalStr: Conduct passive analysis of a publicly documented campaign's domains and certificates; preserve evidence and confidence; avoid unauthorised scanning.
modules.deliverable: Infrastructure relationship graph and reproducible OSINT report.

commands.desc: Enumerate subdomains passively and resolve to active A records
Extract all certificates from Certificate Transparency logs
Discover exposed IP addresses hosting SSL certificates for target
Enumerate all IP prefixes announced by an Autonomous System Number

subtopics.title: Passive DNS & Infrastructure Pivoting
subtopics.detail: Forward DNS, reverse DNS, historic pDNS records, tracking domain name server changes across campaigns, identifying shared bulletproof hosting.

subtopics.title: Certificate Transparency & JARM Fingerprinting
subtopics.detail: Parsing CT logs for pre-issuance staging, JARM active TLS server fingerprinting to detect Cobalt Strike, Mythic, and custom C2 servers.

subtopics.title: Internet-Wide Scanners & OSINT Ethics
subtopics.detail: Querying Shodan, Censys, and BinaryEdge without touching target infrastructure directly; maintaining passive OPSEC.

knowledgeAssessment: How can Certificate Transparency logs reveal adversary staging infrastructure before a phishing campaign launches?
Explain how JARM fingerprints are generated and why identical C2 configurations yield identical hashes.
What is the difference between active reconnaissance and passive threat infrastructure pivoting?
How does an analyst pivot from a single WHOIS registrant email to an entire infrastructure fleet?

modules.title: APT Groups and Campaign Research
modules.whyMatters: Develop a repeatable method for researching named actors and reconstructing campaigns.
modules.topicsStr: Research aliases; attribution caveats; motivation; target sectors; victimology; timelines; initial access; execution; persistence; credential access; discovery; lateral movement; C2; malware; infrastructure; detections; mitigations; competing hypotheses and intelligence gaps.
modules.booksStr: Read MITRE group pages and primary public reporting from CISA, Microsoft, Google Threat Intelligence, Mandiant, ESET and Unit 42. Compare multiple reports rather than trusting a single attribution.
modules.coursesStr: Hackers-Arise: CTI, MITRE ATT&CK, Phishing Analysis and Investigating a Cyber Attack. This is a research-led module, so primary reports matter more than video courses.
modules.practicalStr: Create dossiers for APT28, APT29, Lazarus, APT41, Sandworm and Turla. Distinguish observed facts from vendor assessments.
modules.deliverable: Six evidence-backed actor/campaign dossiers and a comparative analysis.

commands.desc: Query OpenCTI instance for threat actor alias history and attributed malware
Extract exploited CVE identifiers from research whitepaper

subtopics.title: Major APT Profiles & Operational TTPs
subtopics.detail: APT28 (Fancy Bear / GRU), APT29 (Cozy Bear / SVR), Lazarus Group (DPRK RGB), APT41 (Double Dragon / MSS), Sandworm (GRU Unit 74455).

subtopics.title: Campaign Reconstruction Methodology
subtopics.detail: Timeline analysis, identifying initial access vector (spearphishing vs zero-day vs supply chain), tracking persistence mechanisms.

subtopics.title: Intelligence Gaps & Analytical Traps
subtopics.detail: Dealing with missing evidence, distinguishing shared malware builder code from state actor cooperation, false flags in attribution.

knowledgeAssessment: What operational security differences distinguish APT29 from APT28?
How did Sandworm's operations differ between BlackEnergy, NotPetya, and Industroyer?
Why is actor clustering often named differently across commercial security vendors?
What evidence is required to establish high confidence in state-sponsored attribution?

name: Phase 3 · Initial access, identity and enterprise compromise research
goal: Understand identity systems and documented initial-access behaviours from both attacker-research and defensive perspectives.

modules.title: Social Engineering, Phishing and Identity Security
modules.whyMatters: Understand how human and identity attack surfaces are abused and how organisations detect and prevent that abuse.
modules.topicsStr: Phishing, spear phishing, BEC, vishing, smishing, QR phishing, email headers, SMTP, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, attachment and URL analysis, OAuth consent risks, MFA fatigue, AiTM concepts, session tokens, FIDO2, passkeys, WebAuthn, SSO, OAuth, OIDC, SAML, Conditional Access and identity logs.
modules.booksStr: NIST Digital Identity Guidelines; Microsoft Entra identity documentation; MITRE Initial Access; CISA phishing-resistant MFA guidance; OWASP authentication and session guidance.
modules.coursesStr: Hackers-Arise: Phishing Analysis for Security Analyst; The Science and Art of Social Engineering; The Art of Social Engineering in the Era of AI. Use approved simulation platforms and synthetic accounts.
modules.practicalStr: Analyse synthetic phishing messages and headers; review identity sign-in logs; compare password-based MFA with phishing-resistant MFA. Do not deploy credential/session harvesting against real services or people.
modules.deliverable: Email investigation report, identity threat model and phishing-resistant MFA recommendation.

commands.desc: Inspect DNS SPF record policy flags
Verify DKIM DNS selector public key alignment
Extract routing hops, Received headers, and attachments from raw EML

subtopics.title: Email Security Architecture (SPF, DKIM, DMARC)
subtopics.detail: SPF alignment, DKIM cryptographic message signing, DMARC enforcement policies (p=reject, p=quarantine), bounce attacks.

subtopics.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) & Session Theft
subtopics.detail: Reverse proxy credential interceptors (Evilginx concepts), stealing session cookies and bearer tokens to bypass traditional push/SMS MFA.

subtopics.title: Phishing-Resistant MFA & Modern Identity
subtopics.detail: FIDO2 / WebAuthn, hardware authenticators, origin-bound cryptographic challenges, Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies.

knowledgeAssessment: Why does DMARC policy enforcement fail if SPF passes but does not align with the RFC5322 From header?
How does FIDO2 / WebAuthn mathematically prevent Adversary-in-the-Middle proxy attacks?

What telemetry in Entra ID sign-in logs indicates token replay from an anomalous IP?

modules.title: Active Directory and Windows Enterprise Security
modules.whyMatters: Understand enterprise identity, authentication and permission relationships for APT research and authorised assessments.
modules.topicsStr: Domains, forests, trees, OUs, DCs, Global Catalog, DNS, LDAP, Kerberos, NTLM, TGT/TGS, SPN, Group Policy, trusts, replication, FSMO, ACL/DACL/SACL, ACE, service accounts, gMSA, delegation, ADCS, PKI, LAPS, privileged groups, tiered administration, Entra hybrid identity and auditing.

modules.coursesStr: Hackers-Arise: Active Directory for Hackers and PowerShell for Hackers. HTB: Active Directory fundamentals and Active Directory Penetration Tester path. TryHackMe: AD and Windows enterprise rooms.
modules.practicalStr: Build an isolated domain with one Domain Controller and two clients; configure users, groups, GPO and auditing; inspect Kerberos/LDAP evidence; assess and remediate lab misconfigurations.
modules.deliverable: AD architecture diagram, configuration checklist, security assessment and remediation report.

modules.title: APT Execution, Persistence, Lateral Movement and C2 Analysis
modules.whyMatters: Recognise post-compromise behaviours and connect each behaviour to host/network evidence and detection opportunities.

modules.booksStr: MITRE ATT&CK technique pages and detection strategies; Sysmon documentation; Microsoft Sysinternals; Atomic Red Team test documentation; CALDERA documentation.
modules.coursesStr: Hackers-Arise: Red Team Operator Part I, Active Directory, PowerShell and Advanced Linux. Use course material to understand concepts, not as a licence to operate outside a lab.
modules.practicalStr: Run selected safe Atomic Red Team tests on disposable lab endpoints; collect Sysmon and network telemetry; validate detections and document false positives.
modules.deliverable: ATT&CK behaviour-to-telemetry matrix, detection hypotheses and test report.

subtopics.detail: Malleable C2 profiles, jitter calculation, domain fronting concepts, DNS tunneling, multi-tier redirectors, staging payloads.

name: Phase 4 · Malware analysis and reverse engineering
goal: Learn to inspect suspicious files safely, reconstruct program behaviour and produce defensible malware intelligence.

modules.title: Malware Analysis Fundamentals
modules.whyMatters: Understand malware families and analyse files and behaviours safely in an isolated lab.
